title: II-B Key Item Interaction Analysis
use_cases: Use when tracking character-to-object relationships over a specific timeline
Implement when aggregating episode plot points into searchable narrative fragments
Configure when seeking to reduce redundancy in narrative data processing
Use when modeling character emotional changes and item interactions for continuity checks
content: For each episode, we conduct a thorough evaluation by summarizing key plot points, character actions, and tracking interactions with important items. Let Ac​(t)A_{c}(t) represent the actions of character cc at time tt, and let Ii​(t)I_{i}(t) denote interactions with key item ii. The model generates summaries that encapsulate essential elements, including Ac​(t)A_{c}(t) (character actions), relationships, and emotional changes across the episode. It then analyzes the specific interactions Ii​(t)I_{i}(t) between characters and key items, documenting these for further analysis. This step aggregates relevant narrative information—combining episode summaries, key item interactions Ii​(t)I_{i}(t), and character actions Ac​(t)A_{c}(t)—to facilitate more precise future retrieval. The approach simplifies subsequent analysis of plot and item continuity, reducing redundancy and improving efficiency.
